Permutation Index

Source: R/permindex.R
permindex.Rd

This function obtains permutation index for a dataset: free permutations, permutations within blocks, permutations of whole groups (e.g. whole plots), or of whole groups within blocks. The result can be given to permmodels or permlmer (argument perms) for tests that permute only as the design allows (restricted, or design-based, permutation tests).

Usage

permindex(data, block=NULL, group=NULL, nsim=4999, seed)

Arguments

data

Data object used in the model fitting.

block

Name (in "quotes") for the blocking factor in the data.

group

Name (in "quotes") for the group factor in the data.

nsim

The number of permutations. The default is 4999.

seed

Specify a random number generator seed, for reproducible results. The user's random number stream is left as it was.

Value

A matrix with one row per row of data and up to nsim columns, each a permutation of the row numbers of data (row i of the permuted data is row index[i] of data). Duplicated permutations are dropped, so there are fewer columns when the design allows fewer distinct permutations.

Details

Groups are permuted as whole units, so the groups that change places (within a block, if block is given) must have the same number of rows. The data need not be sorted: before predictmeans 2.0 the indices referred to the data sorted by block and group, so they were right only for data already in that order (the permutations are the same as before for sorted data and the same seed).

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

  library(predictmeans)
  block <- rep(1:3, each=12)
  group <- rep(rep(1:3, each=4), 3)
  data <- data.frame(block, group)
  cbind(data, permindex(data, block="block", group="group", nsim=5))

  ## A randomisation test of nitrogen in a randomised block design:
  ## permutations within blocks only
  Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
  fm <- lm(yield ~ Block + nitro, data = Oats)
  idx <- permindex(Oats, block = "Block", nsim = 199, seed = 1)
  permmodels(fm, perms = idx, ncore = 1)
#> 
#> Coefficients of (fixed) effects:
